runners_data.name: Brash

runners_data.name: Ice Show

runners_data.name: Circle Of Trust

races.paceDynamic: Ma Leila represents the only confirmed pace angle and will likely lead uncontested through moderate fractions on good to soft ground. With most runners showing hold-up tendencies (Eagle Bay, Kyrenia, Brash, Ice Show, Dolly Golightly, Soda, Circle Of Trust), there's limited early pace pressure. The two unknown quantities Rake Lane and Revolutionelle could disrupt this, but their lightly raced status suggests they'll likely settle behind the leader. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed to position close to Ma Leila early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If Ma Leila gets an easy lead with the field settling behind her
scenarios.body: The pace will be sustainable allowing her to dictate terms, while the hold-up majority get into a traffic-laden sprint finish. Prominent runners avoid the late carnage and those with early tactical speed can track the leader without pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Unknown Pace Disruptors
scenarios.trigger: If Rake Lane or Revolutionelle show early pace to challenge Ma Leila
scenarios.body: The injection of pace pressure creates a more genuine gallop that will suit horses with stamina and finishing kicks. Hold-up horses get a better setup but the prominent runners may get first run on the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic-Heavy Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches up behind a slow early pace from Ma Leila
scenarios.body: A messy sprint finish develops where positioning and racing room become crucial factors. Horses with the best draws and experienced jockeys gain significant advantages in the final furlong melee.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Ma Leila fails to show her prominent style or gets headed early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a muddling affair with no clear pace angle, creating an unpredictable finish. The most talented horses regardless of style can prevail, but inexperience becomes a major negative factor.

watchPoints.text: Ma Leila's market position will reveal stable confidence after 185-day absence and whether she can reproduce debut promise
Watch for any early pace from Rake Lane or Revolutionelle in the betting or paddock as they could completely change the race dynamics
Eagle Bay's fitness levels after 230 days off will be crucial for a hold-up runner needing to finish strongly
Circle Of Trust showed nursery ability on good to soft going last year but has been disappointing in handicaps this season
The pace through the early stages will determine whether this becomes a tactical affair or genuine test of stamina

races.paceDynamic: Big Shot Veto will lead from the start with no other confirmed front-runners to challenge him early, creating a controlled tempo through the opening stages. The prominent horse Tip Foster may track him closely, while the majority of the field comprises hold-up horses who will need to be delivered late. With soft going at Thirsk's 7f, the pace is likely to quicken from the 3f pole as the hold-up brigade launch their challenges. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed and those capable of prominent positions, as the soft ground and bunched finish will make it difficult for pure hold-up horses to make up significant ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Big Shot Veto maintains a steady gallop and kicks clear approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: The leader's class advantage tells as he controls the race throughout, with soft ground suiting his previous turf form. Hold-up horses struggle to peg back his decisive move in testing conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tip Foster or another forward horse puts pressure on Big Shot Veto from 3f out
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop on soft ground finds out the leader's stamina, allowing a well-positioned tracker to sweep past in the final 100 yards. Forward positioning proves crucial as back-markers can't make up the ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is particularly sedate and the field bunches turning for home
scenarios.body: A strong-staying hold-up horse capitalizes on tactical speed, with the soft ground helping their grinding finish. The race becomes a sprint from 2f out where class and acceleration matter most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Burrows Silver shows natural ability and gets a perfect stalking position
scenarios.body: The well-bred newcomer benefits from race fitness of others fading, with her trainer's poor recent form masking her potential. A patient ride allows her to exploit the closing stages as others tire.

watchPoints.text: Big Shot Veto breaks slowly from the stalls as any tardiness will compromise his front-running tactics completely
Tip Foster gets squeezed for room turning into the straight as his prominent position makes him vulnerable in traffic
Burrows Silver shows early pace despite being a newcomer, which would signal significant ability given her breeding
The pace in the first half-mile becomes overly strong as this would set up the hold-up horses perfectly
Indefensible gets a clear run in the final 2f as his best form suggests he can be competitive with luck

races.paceDynamic: Toptime will lead from the gates with Without Flaw, Zuffolo, Irish Dancer, Miss Rainbow and Kyber Crystal all wanting prominent positions behind him - creating a wall of five horses fighting for the same real estate. This congestion will force some of these to race wider or get shuffled back, with tactical jockeying likely around the 2-3 furlong marker as they sort themselves out. The hold-up horses Beerwah, Keep The Gold and Invincible Crown should get perfect stalking positions behind this early scramble. This pace setup strongly favours the hold-up runners who can avoid the early traffic and produce late kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners clash early and compromise each other in the first two furlongs
scenarios.body: The pace setters will go too hard trying to establish position, setting up perfect conditions for Beerwah and Keep The Gold to sweep past tired leaders. The hold-up runners get clean runs through beaten horses in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Toptime breaks cleanly and the prominent pack hesitates or gets bunched behind him
scenarios.body: Toptime establishes a clear lead while the chasers get in each other's way, giving him enough cushion to hold on. Without Flaw or Irish Dancer could emerge from the pack but too late to catch the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the five prominent runners spread out early and avoid major interference with each other
scenarios.body: The race becomes a straight battle between Irish Dancer, Miss Rainbow and Without Flaw from the 2f pole onwards. One of them times their run perfectly while Toptime fades and the hold-up horses can't make up enough ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Toptime goes too slow early and the prominent runners also hold back waiting
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 2f marker with no established pace, turning into a lottery where any horse with a turn of foot can win. This chaos scenario could throw up an outsider from any position.

watchPoints.text: Watch for serious interference around the 3-2 furlong marker as Without Flaw, Zuffolo, Irish Dancer, Miss Rainbow and Kyber Crystal all converge for prominent positions
Monitor Toptime's early break from the stalls - if he's slow away the prominent pack will swamp him immediately
Keep The Gold showed speed before tiring at Ayr on seasonal return so watch for improved stamina second time back
Irish Dancer carries a 7lb claiming rider into this tactical battle which could prove costly in tight finishes
Watch Aurora's Doublesix early - if she's not traveling smoothly in the first two furlongs she can be dismissed immediately

races.paceDynamic: Taygar is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead with Elvetham the only other horse capable of racing prominently early. With 9 of 11 runners preferring hold-up tactics, this creates a perfect scenario for the lone pace-setter to control fractions without pressure. The lack of early speed means Taygar can dictate a moderate tempo before the cavalry charge arrives in the final 2f. This race shape strongly favours the front runner and any prominent racers who can position close to the pace early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Taygar gets the expected soft lead without early pressure
scenarios.body: The lack of pace competition allows him to control fractions and kick clear when the hold-up brigade are still making ground. His recent runner-up efforts show he's knocking on the door and this tactical advantage could be decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their ideal scenario with a slowly-run race that turns into a dash. Fresh legs and finishing speed become paramount over positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Taygar goes too slow early and gets swamped by superior horses
scenarios.body: The tempo becomes unsustainably slow allowing the better-rated hold-up horses to showcase their class. Position becomes irrelevant in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Success
scenarios.trigger: If Elvetham can sit second and outkick Taygar in the straight
scenarios.body: The second-string pace horse gets the perfect trip tracking the leader before showing superior finishing speed. Recent Lingfield win shows he can capitalize when positioned well.

watchPoints.text: Taygar must break cleanly to secure uncontested lead - any slow start ruins his tactical advantage completely
Watch for Elvetham's positioning in first furlong - if he sits close second this becomes tactical battle between two
Imperial Guard wearing visor for first time - any positive headgear response could unlock improvement after poor seasonal return
Fan Mail's cheekpieces worked last time when just held - another step forward makes him dangerous from rear
Monitor early pace through first 2f - if Taygar goes too slowly the hold-up horses get ideal setup for late charge

races.name: Ruby Lodge Care Home In Thirsk Handicap

runners_data.name: Myrrh
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won on soft ground at Hamilton, needs strong pace to be effective but Oisin Orr knows him well from recent rides
runners_data.comment: Hamilton maiden winner (8.5f); twice placed since, including at Doncaster (1m2f) in April.
runners_data.spotlight: Carried persistently left when awarded the race at Hamilton (8.5f, maiden) last September; twice placed since, including when third on handicap debut at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) in April; latest Redcar fourth was broadly similar on RPRs; new trip but considered.

runners_data.name: King Of Berkshire
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who can control the tempo, McDonald's 5lb claim valuable and horse showed staying power when winning at Redcar over 1m2f
runners_data.comment: Redcar winner (1m2f); in the mix at Windsor since and this looks a good opportunity.
runners_data.spotlight: Knuckled down to score at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm; 5-6 favourite) on penultimate start and in the mix from this revised mark at Windsor (11.5f; third) subsequently; few concerns about 1m4f around this sharp track, so this looks a good opportunity to add to his tally.

runners_data.name: Rumbustious
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who may track King Of Berkshire early, lacks a recent win but Charlie Johnston's 14-day runners have been competitive
runners_data.comment: Lacked the necessary gears when fourth of 11 at Haydock (1m2f; 20-1) latest; new trip.
runners_data.spotlight: Stayed on into third in a Chelmsford maiden (1m2f, AW) in March and again lacked the necessary gears when fourth of 11 at Haydock (1m2f, good to soft; 20-1) a fortnight ago on second handicap start; still unexposed and this extra two furlongs is worth a go.

runners_data.name: Fareenar
runners_data.note: Hold-up type equipped with tongue-tie, running off a 2lb lower mark than recent efforts but form has declined since going handicapping
runners_data.comment: Has gone backwards since introduced to tongue-tie and sent handicapping
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in a Redcar novice (1m, good; 16-1) last October but has gone backwards since introduced to a tongue-tie and sent handicapping; 2lb lower than when sixth of nine at Beverley (1m2f, good to firm) latest; new trip.

runners_data.name: Wave Power
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs everything to fall right, 37 days since last run suggests freshening up after winter gelding operation
runners_data.spotlight: Initial promise when a never-nearer fourth to Myrrh at Hamilton (8.5f, soft) last September; gelded over the winter and struggled to get competitive on handicap debut at Southwell (1m3f, AW; 40-1) five weeks ago, beaten over 15l; others are more obvious candidates.

runners_data.name: Forever Perfect
runners_data.note: Strong AW form this spring but unproven on turf, needs patient ride from back and strong gallop to be effective
runners_data.comment: Career best when second to progressive Kakirra (won twice since) at Wolverhampton latest.
runners_data.spotlight: Productive on AW this spring (form figures 3122); career best when runner-up to the progressive Kakirra (won twice since) at Wolverhampton (1m4f; from 2lb lower) four weeks ago; needs to prove herself conclusively on turf but this sharp left-handed track looks suitable.

races.paceDynamic: King Of Berkshire will lead from the start with no serious pace pressure, allowing him to dictate terms at his preferred tempo. The prominent runner Rumbustious may track him early, but the majority of the field (Myrrh, Fareenar, Wave Power, Forever Perfect) are hold-up performers who will settle behind and rely on late runs. With just one genuine front-runner against four hold-up horses, the pace will likely be modest through the early stages before quickening late. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and prominent racers who can avoid traffic problems and capitalize on the lack of early pace pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If King Of Berkshire gets his own way in front without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: McDonald can dictate a steady gallop and have enough left to repel late challenges, especially with his proven ability at this trip. The hold-up horses will find the modest pace insufficient to set up their finishing kicks effectively.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too slow and allows closers to unleash strong finishing efforts
scenarios.body: Myrrh and Forever Perfect will benefit from the patient tactics, with Myrrh's Hamilton win proving his effectiveness on similar ground. The front-runner may tie up after dictating throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Works
scenarios.trigger: If Rumbustious or another forward runner applies early pressure to King Of Berkshire
scenarios.body: The increased gallop will set up the race for those tracking just behind the leaders, with Rumbustious positioned to strike. King Of Berkshire may crack under sustained pressure having to work harder early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the favorites fail to handle the soft ground or tactical complications arise
scenarios.body: Wave Power or Fareenar could benefit from a truly-run race if connections have found improvement since their last runs. Traffic problems in a small field could also create unexpected opportunities for patient rides.

watchPoints.text: King Of Berkshire breaking slowly or being bustled early would completely change the pace dynamic and favour the hold-up horses
Myrrh drifting left under pressure as he did when winning at Hamilton, could cause interference in the straight
Forever Perfect adapting to turf having shown best form on artificial surfaces this season
Rumbustious being too keen early and pressing King Of Berkshire harder than ideal, potentially compromising both their chances
The pace through the first half-mile, as a truly steady tempo will make it very difficult for the hold-up horses to close effectively

races.name: David Ritchie Is 50! Happy Birthday! Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits this pace setup perfectly but has pulled too hard in recent starts which could negate tactical advantage
runners_data.comment: 1-7; raced wide at Catterick latest and may well come from that reappearance; back to 5f.
runners_data.spotlight: Improved when winning a handicap at Leicester (6f, good to soft) in September but pulled too hard at Newcastle next time; beat only one rival home at Catterick (6f, good) on her reappearance but she raced wide on that occasion and may well come on for it; drop back to 5f should be fine.

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with poor turf record returning from wind operation but positioned well tactically for late charge
runners_data.comment: All four wins have been on the AW; down the field on her stable debut at Redcar last month
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins have been on the AW and she's yet to finish in the first three in four races on turf; pulled up after hitting the gates on her final start for David O'Meara and needs to take a step forward from last month's stable debut.

runners_data.name: Fille Unique
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts her in the danger zone but recent good form and Paul Mulrennan booking significant positives
runners_data.comment: Off the mark when winning at Musselburgh in April and went close last time; 2lb well in
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the eighth attempt when winning at Musselburgh (5f, good) in April and went close off this mark at Redcar (5f, good to firm) 11 days ago; 2lb well in and has solid claims.

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who made all last time but now faces much stiffer pace competition in early stages
runners_data.comment: Made all at Nottingham last month and now 6lb higher; can give another good account
runners_data.spotlight: Posted some solid efforts in handicaps prior to getting off the mark at Nottingham (5f, good) 27 days ago, making all; now 6lb higher but she's likely to give another good account.

runners_data.name: Thunder Star
runners_data.note: Prominent style with veteran's racecraft but 55-day break and poor recent form major concerns
runners_data.comment: Has won five times on turf; failed to beat a rival at Yarmouth latest; switch of headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Has won five times on turf on a variety of ground; did best of her group when ninth of 17 at Doncaster (5f, good to soft) on her return but failed to beat a rival home at Yarmouth 55 days ago; blinkers replace cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Military Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited and recent winner showing improved form under Connor Beasley
runners_data.comment: Built on her return when winning at Ayr last time (good to firm); claims back up 5lb
runners_data.spotlight: Built on her reappearance when beating her five rivals at Ayr (5f, good to firm) 16 days ago; won a maiden on good to soft in 2024 and has claims back up 5lb.

runners_data.name: Tanjen
runners_data.note: Lone leader will dictate terms but both wins came on all-weather surfaces raising turf effectiveness questions
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins have been on the AW (2-3 in that sphere); did best of the group of four at Goodwood (5f, good) on her reappearance but failed to back that up at Beverley (5f, good to firm) 24 days ago; needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: J Street
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts her in traffic danger and sole win came on soft ground over year ago
runners_data.comment: 1-13; shaped well at Doncaster in March and another solid effort on the AW last time
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win from 13 starts came in a maiden at Catterick (5f, soft) in July 2024; shaped well when sixth of 17 at Doncaster (5f, good to soft) in March and ran another solid race on the AW at Southwell 15 days ago; contender.

runners_data.name: Data Fata Secutus
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with visor fitted returning quickly after yesterday's run showing connections' confidence
runners_data.comment: Recent efforts suggest that this extra half furlong will be a positive; visored; player.
runners_data.spotlight: Placed at Musselburgh (5f, good) and Redcar (5f, good to firm) in two of her four starts on turf this season; not so good in the other two, however, and she weakened tamely when a visor was added at Wetherby on Thursday.

runners_data.name: Star Marian
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but better needed after 18-day break following poor recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Made all in a maiden at Wolverhampton in March but well held in two AW handicaps since
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in a maiden at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) in March but she's been well held in two handicaps since; better needed back on turf.

runners_data.name: Solid Bond
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 221 days off following wind operation with unproven current fitness
runners_data.comment: Placed twice at novice level but didn't progress in handicaps; wind operation since
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice at novice level, including on soft ground over this C&D on her debut, but wasn't able to progress in handicaps last year; has had a wind operation since last seen 221 days ago and she's best watched unless the market speaks favourably.

runners_data.name: Cheerleader
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 291-day absence makes her extremely hard to assess despite previous course form
runners_data.comment: Won twice last May but didn't beat a rival when last seen 291 days ago; wind operation
runners_data.spotlight: Won her first two starts for this yard at Redcar (good to firm) and Catterick (good to soft) last May, but she was last of eight at the latter track when last seen 291 days ago; has since had wind surgery.

races.paceDynamic: Tanjen is the lone confirmed front-runner and will set the early fractions without pressure, creating a sustainable gallop early. Five horses (Fille Unique, Dragon Spin, Thunder Star, J Street, Data Fata Secutus) want prominent positions, creating significant traffic problems and interference from 2f out as they jostle for racing room. The hold-up brigade (Pull The Rug, Startling, Military Girl, Star Marian) will have clear runs through gaps as the prominent runners compromise each other. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can exploit the carnage ahead and time their challenges late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quintet gets bunched and creates interference from 2f out
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses find clear runs through the chaos while the prominent runners compromise each other's finishing efforts. Military Girl and Pull The Rug benefit most from their patient tactics and ability to quicken late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dragon Spin Escapes Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If Dragon Spin secures the ideal prominent position just behind Tanjen without getting boxed
scenarios.body: She avoids the worst of the traffic while the other four prominent runners interfere with each other, allowing her recent winner's form to shine through. Fille Unique could follow her through if timing the move perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tanjen Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners neutralize each other early through over-racing and positioning battles
scenarios.body: The lone leader maintains her advantage as the chasers waste energy fighting for position rather than chasing the pace. Thunder Star's experience could see her emerge from the pack late but too late to catch the leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Creates Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If severe interference occurs in the straight affecting multiple fancied runners
scenarios.body: An unfancied runner like Data Fata Secutus or Solid Bond capitalizes on their low draw and finds racing room while others are stopped in their tracks. Cheerleader's return from a long break could catch tired legs.

watchPoints.text: Watch for severe interference from 2f out when Fille Unique, Dragon Spin, Thunder Star, J Street and Data Fata Secutus converge
Monitor if Tanjen can maintain her kick on turf having shown best form on all-weather surfaces
Check if Pull The Rug settles early or pulls too hard again which would ruin her tactical advantage
Observe Data Fata Secutus running yesterday then backing up today with visor applied for first time
Watch Solid Bond's fitness levels after 221-day break following wind operation

races.name: Next Meeting Tuesday 16th June Featuring Royal Ascot Handicap

runners_data.name: Real Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making handicap debut after 29 days off, needs pace to aim at and may struggle for room in a big field
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Newcastle in November; ran to a similar level in both starts this year (AW)
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 but runner-up in a novice at Newcastle (5f, AW) in November; midfield finish on handicap debut at Southwell (6f, AW) in April and ran to a similar level there (7f) four weeks ago; drops back in trip on this return to turf.

runners_data.name: Brave Traveller
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist returning to turf after AW success, likely to make all or bust trying
runners_data.comment: Won at Newcastle in December and went close there last time after being gelded; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 6f nursery at Newcastle in December and went close there last time over 5f on his first start since being gelded; steps back up in trip and returns to turf; can make his presence felt.

runners_data.name: Empress Olivia
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid soft ground form including a course win, well-suited to conditions
runners_data.comment: Both wins over 6f at Ripon; possibly wasn't helped by track position at Ascot last time
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins have been over 6f at Ripon, the most recent in April on good to soft off 4lb lower than today; led a smaller group of five when 11th at Ascot (6f, good) 28 days ago but looks capable of bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Bye Law
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling to recapture juvenile form in handicaps, needs everything to fall right
runners_data.comment: Won a Ayr maiden and Redcar novice last summer but hasn't matched that level since
runners_data.spotlight: Won Ayr maiden and Redcar novice (6f, good/good to firm) last summer but he hasn't matched that level in handicaps since; never-dangerous sixth of 14 at Beverley (5f, good to soft) last month but well held over 7f at York 13 days ago; drops back to 6f with a place squeak.

runners_data.name: Showtown
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong soft ground record but carrying first-time cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: Ran better at Haydock last time than he did on his handicap debut; better is still needed
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field on his handicap debut at Beverley (5f, good to soft; first-time cheekpieces) last month but ran a bit better when fourth of 11 at Haydock (6f, soft) 15 days ago; better still needed.

runners_data.name: Logi Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has struggled since yard switch, needs significant pace collapse
runners_data.comment: Sole win came at Newmarket last May; not threatened in two starts since joining stable
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win from 12 starts came for Richard Hannon at Newmarket (6f, good) last May; struggled on his last few starts for that stable and he's not threatened in his two outings since joining this yard; dropped another 3lb.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning after 253-day break but has course form and should be ready
runners_data.comment: 0-4; below his best at Pontefract when last seen 253 days ago and has since been gelded
runners_data.spotlight: 0-4 but he did finish in the first three in each of his first three starts, including over C&D in August; below his best at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) when last seen 253 days ago and has since been gelded; handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: Prominent racer making turf debut after three AW seconds, unknown on this surface
runners_data.comment: Second in his first three starts (AW) but well beaten on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Second in his first three starts (6f/5f, AW) but finished down the field in a competitive race at York (5f, good) on his handicap and turf debut three weeks ago; steps back up in trip and drops in grade.

runners_data.name: Daizen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with soft ground win but inconsistent recent form
runners_data.comment: Sole win came in a soft-ground maiden at Ayr; a bit better than the bare result last time
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win from nine starts came in a maiden at Ayr (6f, soft) in September; below that level since but he shaped a bit better than the bare result at Haydock (6f, soft) 15 days ago; each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Perineighs
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning after 219-day break, trip drop may suit but fitness unclear
runners_data.comment: Solid effort when third on her handicap debut at Nottingham (5f) in October; back up to 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden but she posted a solid effort when third of nine on her handicap debut at Nottingham (5f, soft) in October; off since but should be suited by the step back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Different Opinions
runners_data.note: Prominent racer making handicap debut with visor fitted, showed early promise
runners_data.comment: Promising second on his debut in March but hasn't progressed; visor now added
runners_data.spotlight: Promising second on his debut at Chelmsford (7f, AW) in March but he's not progressed in three starts since, including over this trip at Ripon in April; makes his handicap debut with a visor now applied.

runners_data.name: Uncertainty
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling since trainer switch, needs strong pace but yard form poor
runners_data.comment: 0-9; struggled in three starts since joining this stable (1m/6f) and has a bit to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Nine-race maiden who was runner-up at Lingfield (7f, AW) on her final outing for Richard Hannon; however, she's struggled in three starts for this yard (1m/6f) and has a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Hvar
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with one AW win but poor recent handicap form since joining new stable
runners_data.comment: Won a 6f novice on the AW for Ralph Beckett; struggled in handicaps for this stable
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the third attempt when winning a novice at Wolverhampton (6f) in October on his final start for Ralph Beckett, but he's struggled in three handicaps since joining this stable; others have stronger claims.

races.paceDynamic: Napolian and Brave Traveller will contest the early lead, with Napolian having previously led over course and distance and Brave Traveller being a confirmed front-runner who won when making all at Newcastle. The prominent runners Empress Olivia, Showtown, Von Trotter, Daizen and Hvar should track the leaders closely on the good to soft ground over this sharp 6f trip. With multiple hold-up horses including Real Jack, Bye Law, Logi Bear, Perineighs and Uncertainty needing to make up ground, and the testing conditions favouring those who can secure good positions early, this race strongly favours prominent racers and front-runners who can avoid traffic problems.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Napolian and Brave Traveller establish a clear lead without burning each other up early.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes steady enough for the leaders to maintain their advantage, with the testing ground making it difficult for hold-up horses to quicken decisively. Empress Olivia and Showtown can track them into contention but the leaders prove strongest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners go too hard early and compromise each other.
scenarios.body: Empress Olivia, Showtown or Von Trotter can sit in the perfect stalking position behind the pace duel. The good to soft ground aids their stamina while the early leaders fade, allowing the prominent racers to strike in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely with minimal early speed despite the front-runners.
scenarios.body: Real Jack, Bye Law or Logi Bear get the slow pace they need to unleash their finishing kicks. The soft ground plays to their stamina strengths while the lack of early pace allows them to get competitive positions without using too much energy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems or uneven pace creates gaps for tactical horses.
scenarios.body: The moderate pace and soft ground creates a messy race where positioning becomes crucial. Different Opinions or Hvar can exploit gaps while others get caught in trouble, benefiting from their tactical speed rather than pure pace position.

watchPoints.text: Napolian and Brave Traveller could burn each other up if they engage in a speed duel from the start
Real Jack and other hold-up horses may get caught in traffic in a competitive 13-runner handicap
Von Trotter makes his turf debut after three AW seconds and his surface adaptation is unknown
Perineighs returns after 219 days off which raises serious fitness concerns despite previous ability
Several horses including Showtown and Different Opinions sport new headgear suggesting trainer concerns
